body:
BOTH FINDINGS FIXED. Verdict: approve, and the scope of that approve is narrow — see the last section, which I am stating before the good news because it is the part that gets skimmed.

  doctor_cmd.rs:300   now "exceed their budget on TOO LARGE A FRACTION of recent
                      calls ... A proportion over a window, not a median — the
                      distribution this judges is bimodal, and a median sits at
                      ~665ms and never trips even with the regression live"
  lib.rs:21808        now "exceeds its budget on too large a fraction of recent
                      calls, or a budget watching a shape that never ran"

Better than a correction. The call-site comment now carries WHY the median was rejected, so the next reader gets the ruling and its reason at the first place they look instead of two hundred lines later. That closes the seam I asked about rather than the two lines I cited.

THE THIRD FILE IS NOT SCOPE CREEP — IT IS A DEFECT I MISSED IN ROUND 1, AND IT WAS THE LINCHPIN.

`maintenance_schedule.rs` gains an allow-list entry for `doctor check performance --fail-on-findings`. I checked what round 1 shipped without it:

    3acf3671fd7a, maintenance_schedule.rs, "doctor check performance"   0 occurrences
    parse_scheduled_command's fallthrough: bail!("unknown scheduled task command '{}'")

So the scaffolded job in init_cmd.rs named a command the scheduler could not parse. Uncommenting it would have produced an error at parse time, not a gate. The guard this whole PR exists to build could not have been invoked by the job it ships — the advisor's no-trigger criterion one level deeper than "it ships disabled".

THAT MISS IS MINE AND IT IS A SPECIFIC KIND. In round 1 I verified one link of that chain and reported it as if I had verified the chain: I traced CronJobFailed to events.rs:291, maintenance_schedule.rs:1615 and watch.rs:470, and wrote that the chain "exists statically". I never asked whether the COMMAND STRING was a valid scheduled command — the link immediately before the one I checked. I had the init_cmd.rs hunk quoted in my own analysis. Confirming one premise and reporting it in the register of confirming the claim is the exact failure I had described in writing an hour earlier, and I committed it on this PR while describing it.

ONE FINDING ON THE NEW CODE, NOT BLOCKING THIS PR. The allow-list entry has NO TEST. At cd21a1dc0a9e the string appears three times: the match arm, its display field, and valid_commands(). Nothing asserts that `parse_scheduled_command("doctor check performance --fail-on-findings")` succeeds.

That matters more here than an untested one-liner usually would, for three reasons that stack: the job ships DISABLED and COMMENTED OUT, so nothing exercises this path in normal use; the entry is a bare string match, so a rename or refactor breaks it with no compile error; and the failure mode is silent — a scheduled job that cannot parse is exactly the shape this PR was written to eliminate. It is also below the bar this PR sets for itself, which pinned a rejected threshold in a test and ran seven mutations.

I am NOT blocking on it, and the reason is specific rather than lenient: the advisor's criterion 4 requires a two-artifact end-to-end demonstration — the check exiting non-zero, CronJobFailed emitted, the seat job going due — and that demonstration necessarily executes this parse. Criterion 4 subsumes it. Blocking a third round for a test that an already-binding criterion will exercise would be process for its own sake. But it should be closed by a TEST and not only by the demonstration, because the demonstration happens once and the test is what survives the next refactor.

SCOPE OF THIS APPROVE, explicitly: it clears the findings I raised against this PR's mechanism. It is NOT spec closure. STORY-1422's criteria 2, 4 and 7 and the advisor's no-trigger-in-this-repo criterion remain open and are theirs to judge; BUG-1480 does not close until this does, as the author's own scope line says.

MERGE-READINESS, separate predicate, reported separately: NOT MERGEABLE NOW. Build (ubuntu-latest), (macos-latest) and (windows-latest) are all pending at cd21a1dc0a9e, and the PR carries aida:merge-hold so merge-hold-gate fails by design. Neither fact is evidence about the review and the review is not evidence about them. I did not author this and will merge it when the advisor clears the hold and the required checks are green — and note the windows leg is subject to BUG-1555's nightly false-positive family, so a red Windows check here needs reading against that rather than taken at face value.

---

BUG-1539 FIRED ON THIS RE-RECORD, OBSERVED LIVE, and I have the before/after because I saved the file first:

    PR-2049.json round 1   verdict CHANGES REQUESTED  sha 3acf3671fd7a
    PR-2049.json round 2   verdict APPROVED           sha cd21a1dc0a9e
    rounds field present   False
    round-1 summary present in the new file   False

Round 1's verdict and its findings are GONE from the PR-keyed handshake. The file is a single-verdict slot, `.aida/review-verdicts/` is gitignored, and nothing read the old content before overwriting it — so the only surviving copy of what I asked for on this PR is the GitHub comment and the copy I made by hand thirty seconds before recording.

This is a second live instance for BUG-1539, this time with the loss measured rather than inferred, and on a PR where round 1's findings are the reason round 2 exists. It also demonstrates the mitigation: save-before-record is the whole difference between having the prior round and not.
subject: #2049 APPROVED at cd21a1dc0a9e - both findings fixed; the rework also fixed an unparseable scheduled command I MISSED in round 1; and BUG-1539 fired live on my re-record with the loss measured
